sources.title: Updates on the move to eVisas
sources.officialityEvidence: The live UKVI transition notice was updated on 1 July 2026. It states both the successful-application eVisa outcome and the date new physical visa vignettes stopped.
sources.supportingExcerpt: UKVI stopped issuing visa vignette (stickers) to successful new applicants on 1 July 2026.

sources.title: eVisas: access and use your online immigration status
sources.officialityEvidence: The current GOV.UK eVisa service defines an eVisa as the digital record of identity, immigration status and conditions obtained after a successful visa or permission application.
sources.supportingExcerpt: You'll get an eVisa when you successfully apply for a visa or other type of permission to be in the UK.

policies.title: United Kingdom visa-national ordinary passports: digitally issued Standard Visitor visa
policies.summary: The exact current visa-national ordinary-passport cohort still needs individual entry clearance before travel, but every successful new application is now issued as an eVisa rather than a passport vignette.
conditions: The policy covers the current Visa National List's ordinary-passport Standard Visitor baseline. Its document-specific exceptions, organised school parties, airside transit and special or non-national travel documents are not flattened into the nationality rows.

A visa remains individually adjudicated before travel. Applicants apply online, pay the fee, provide supporting documents and normally attend a visa application centre to provide fingerprints and a photograph; electronic issuance does not make this an ETA or visa-free route.
UKVI stopped issuing new visa vignette stickers on 1 July 2026. Successful applicants access the eVisa through a UKVI account and must link the passport or accepted travel document used for travel.

A person whose passport or travel document is not accepted by the Home Office may receive a physical Form for Accompanying an eVisa. The form enables travel with the linked eVisa and does not turn the visa into a vignette-issued route.

Physical vignettes issued before the cutover remain valid until their individual expiry. The 25 February 2026 partial rollout is retained as historical context but is not assigned by nationality because the official announcement defined only most visitor applicants.
Marriage or civil-partnership visits, longer stays, work, study, residence, settlement, transit and final border admission remain outside this ordinary short-visitor classification.

application.label: UK Standard Visitor visa official application
application.processingTime: The Home Office normally states three weeks after the online application, identity proof and document submission, although individual cases can take longer.
steps: Confirm that the passport is visa-national and that Standard Visitor is the correct route.
Apply online before travel, pay the fee and submit the required supporting evidence.
Attend the instructed visa application-centre appointment to provide the passport, fingerprints and photograph.
After approval, link the travel document to the UKVI account, check the eVisa and travel only while the permission is valid.
